Good morning my people! It's 2026 and we had our massive "blue tsunami" election result and I'm going to take a few minutes to write out what I'm processing - its been a typically busy week and I haven't reflected much on how big this election has been. I decided to write this above Bernie's post because he's one of the ones who is like a north star, consistently saying what I believe we need to do to make things OK for all of us in the long term. But lets hit pause for a minute on the jersey color of “blue” I referenced – more on that. Folks, this is a MUCH BIGGER WIN than we could have ever dared to dream! We WON! WE DID IT! But what did we enable with this win? What next? Many people I know in my little slice of the world have worked very, very hard to make this happen. Most of you all worked harder than I did, I really didn’t do more than I could manage. Nobody needs to feel like they didn’t do enough – we all do what we can do. I am grateful to you all. And many of you are now my new friends here on social media! I meet the nicest people being active in community politics! I cherish that and never expected it when I walked into an Indivisible meeting in April 2025. So when you read about a blue tsunami, I know this is because of countless local circles like ours, organizing for something better as a reaction to MAGA neo-fascism. And I hope and pray, that like the people I know and have talked to since the election, this won’t stop with one “blue wave”...and it isn’t really about pushing back on MAGA. We need to keep our eyes steady on the horizon and step high, keep our eyes on the prize. We need to do so much more than just put some Democrats in office for a while. We need to secure the blessings of liberty for ourselves and our posterity. This means that the “blue” vs “red” thing needs to be cut down. In my local congressional district, Laubacher v Boebert, the margin of victory for Laubacher looks to be less that 1%. But there is a Libertarian, Doug Mangeris, who got about 3%, enough to swing the election either way. I’ve been thinking about those libertarians, what are they saying with their vote? And also about why people voted MAGA twice now. That’s a signal that we’ve got big problems from this 2 party system, people aren’t heard, their values aren’t reflected in either party, and for damn sure the government and our system of corrupt capitalism isn’t delivering for them in their everyday lives. That’s what Bernie is saying below here. Remember Bernie is an independent. We need independence from this two party system. Y’all, this isn’t as hard as it sounds. I think about really fixing what’s wrong with our country and I get this feeling of impossibility, either because nobody knows how to or it would never happen because big changes haven’t happened in my entire life. But that’s what they want us to feel! It’s self defeating, self-sabotaging hopelessness. As to “how” to fix stuff, well read the short little list Bernie gives you below, it ain’t that damn hard to understand. That is pretty much it! The one thing he doesn’t mention though goes back to those Libertarians, and all those many, many independent voters who aren’t on team blue or red. We need to break down this two party system, where the R’s play the social and fiscal conservatives (lies OFC) and the D’s play the tolerant and compassionate ones (are they really?). This is a good cop/bad cop routine. They both serve corporate and Epstein class interests in their own way. The R’s win a 4-8 year cycle, and then the D’s come in as the saviors. But the mainstream D’s are ineffective captured opposition. They play-act as foil to the R’s. They don’t deliver on making things better for working families, so back come the R’s in the next round. Round and round she goes. Stay in government as long as Chuck Schumer or Mitch McConnell has and you see this ebb and flow as regular as the tide. Meantime you and me and everyone we know gets squeezed by the corrupt corporations consolidating their power over the economy more and more. Both parties are owned by the corporations and the billionaires. I registered Democrat this year in order to vote in the primaries, and push candidates who are NOT mainstream Dems. People who really want to represent their constituents and don’t take dark money. This isn’t that hard either. Get back to representing the people that elected you and not the money that funds your next campaign. But I’m not really a Democrat – I’m independent and will do whatever is strategically necessary to fix this broken 2 party system. How do we dilute the power of the 2 party system? We could have ranked choice voting. We could see smaller parties or independents winning more local, then national, offices. We could make it necessary for parties to form coalitions in order to govern. Funding elections publicly will make smaller parties better able to compete. So what Bernie says about getting rid of big money gets us down that road. Independents, libertarians, I hear you. This “blue wave” is for you too. Its not really blue, it’s for everybody, even people who still think the Republicans somehow have their back. If we allow the “blue wave” to just become another turn of the same old wheel, then we haven’t delivered on what I and all our friends have been pulling for. Let use this huge moment to make a crack in that wheel. Keep on keeping on my friends! Eyes on the prize! # uspol # indivisible # bluewave
